title: QUANTGEN live paper test 2: KOSPI hours
subtitle: Run 2: 2026-10-12, 10:19–15:20 KST (KRX to the closing auction, plus CME futures and FX). Compared with Run 1: 2026-10-07, 21:01–01:42 KST (US/UK markets and FICC). Same five $500 accounts and account rules; the engine gained a currency translator and KRX session hours. Simulated fills on Yahoo prices.
summary: The five accounts lost $7.47 of $2,500 (−0.30%), against $17.32 (−0.69%) in Run 1. Almost all of the improvement is cheaper trading, not better prediction: costs fell from $15.91 to $5.56, while P&L before costs was −$1.91, slightly worse than Run 1's −$1.41. The average cost per trade fell from $0.156 to $0.062 because QUANTGEN's own KRX ETF rate is 3 bp a side, against 50 bp for US ETFs and LSE shares bought through KIS.

The same two accounts lost the most, now in the other order (LAZYOWEN-NAIVE first, QG-TREND second), QG-TACTICAL again refused every trade (104 cost-gate refusals; the best expected move was 4.1 bp), and QG-CORE moved with its markets. Korean shares fell during the window (KODEX KOSDAQ150 −1.52%, Samsung Electronics −1.52%), so the risk-budgeted basket, which ended flat in Run 1, lost $1.08. LAZYOWEN-CAL made its first trade of either run.

equity_note: P&L against the $500 start, marked every 5 minutes (KST). Run 1's QG-TREND staircase came from 50 bp LSE and ETF round trips; in Run 2 most of its KRX trades were 3 bp ETFs and most of its $2.05 of costs came from FX and CME, so its line ends at −$2.17 instead of −$10.27. The dashed line is the equal-weight buy-and-hold basket of each run's universe, with no costs: −$0.32 in Run 1 and −$1.13 in Run 2.
differences: QG-TREND lost $2.17 instead of $10.27, with 16 trades instead of 25; its costs fell from $8.82 to $2.05. Its four KRX trades (three ETFs and one KB Financial share trade) cost $0.46 in total, against $6.40 for nine LSE trades in Run 1. The costliest venue is now FX: two EUR/USD positions of about $175 paid $0.70 at 10 bp a side.
The market leg turned against QG-CORE.

Its basket moved from seven CME futures to KRX ETFs plus ES and ZN. KOSDAQ150 (−$0.56) and KODEX 200 (−$0.25) lost as Korean shares fell, and the 10-year KTB ETF (+$0.27) partly offset them. Net −$1.08, at the 24th percentile of its KRX replay.

In its out-of-sample window the refitted FX model reached the 8 pp edge 108 times (3 times in Run 1). Live, it bought AUD/USD at p = 0.58 and exited on edge decay 20 minutes later: $0.00 before costs, $0.06 of cost.
Inverse ETFs became a real short route.

LAZYOWEN-NAIVE shorted 13 times through KODEX Inverse, KODEX KOSDAQ150 Futures Inverse and KODEX USD Futures Inverse (once in Run 1, through RWM). These trades lost $0.76, $0.53 of it before costs. The flat 3 bp rate understates QUANTGEN's own tick-floor cost on low-priced inverse ETFs (about 6–12 bp), by roughly $0.36 across these trades.
Korean single stocks are the expensive corner.
At 35 bp a side, LAZYOWEN-NAIVE's three KOSPI stock trades (Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, KB Financial) lost $1.11, of which $0.63 was cost.
LAZYOWEN-NAIVE again exited 57 of 67 trades on the 5 pp edge-decay rule, with an average hold of 22 minutes.

There was no change during the run (Run 1 was patched at 21:17 KST). One download dropped the KODEX Gold ETF at 13:30; the carry-forward added after Run 1's review kept the books valid. All 12 controls passed, none with an exception.
replay_intro: Each run's rules were replayed over recent sessions in the same clock window, with live-like delays (KRX 20 minutes). Replay losses are smaller in the KRX window for QG-TREND, QG-CORE and LAZYOWEN-NAIVE. For QG-TREND and LAZYOWEN-NAIVE the improvement matches the cost cut; QG-CORE's is mostly market P&L. LAZYOWEN-CAL's small loss grew (−$0.01 to −$0.04 a session) because it traded more often. P&L before costs stays at zero within noise in both (the largest |t| across the 14 KRX grid variants is 1.8).
lessons: Confirmed: there is no predictive edge.
P&L before costs was −$1.41 and −$1.91 in the two sessions, and every replay and grid variant is flat before costs. Changing markets did not change this.
Confirmed: turnover times cost decides the result, and the cost gate is the component that works.
Without its gate, QG-TACTICAL loses $2.40 a session in the KRX replay ($3.87 in Run 1's).
New: venue choice matters about as much as the best parameter.

Moving the same rules from 50 bp venues to 3 bp KRX ETFs cut the live loss by 57% and the replay losses of QG-TREND and LAZYOWEN-NAIVE by about half. For QG-TREND, slower bars matter even more: 30-minute bars cut the KRX replay loss from −$4.05 to −$1.58 a session (−$1.48 with hysteresis also raised to 0.4), but never above zero.

For a Korean account, route short-horizon risk to KRX ETFs and KOSPI 200 futures, which QUANTGEN's KIS layer already quotes. Keep single stocks and large FX tickets out of short-horizon rules, charge inverse ETFs QUANTGEN's tick-floor cost, and translate KRW at each price bar's own time.
limits: Two five-hour sessions are two data points, not a validation; QUANTGEN's own gate needs 100+ trades over years. Fills used Yahoo's last 1-minute close (KRX about 20 minutes late, CME about 10), so the 15:20 flatten priced KRX at roughly 15:00 quotes. KRW was translated at the current USD/KRW rather than at each price bar's time, which adds about 7 bp of noise per leg on average (up to about 18 bp). Futures and FX are CFD-style synthetic exposures; a $500 cash account cannot hold a CME contract.

errataIntro: This edition corrects the report first published on 2026-10-12. Both sessions' trades, P&L and costs are unchanged. What changed:

KODEX KOSDAQ150 fell 1.52% (was 1.48%) and Samsung Electronics 1.52% (was 1.32%).
Ties now count as half: QG-TACTICAL, which never traded, sits at the 50th percentile in both runs (was 0th); LAZYOWEN-CAL on Oct 7 at the 56th (was 12th).
Translating KRW at the fill's clock time instead of the price bar's time adds about 7 bp per leg on average, up to about 18 bp (was 'about 8, up to about 15').
